# Expected results for the Framework v1 verification of Mozart, Piano Sonata in C major K. 545, first movement.
#
# SOURCE: the Neue Mozart-Ausgabe (IX/25/2) and the IMSLP scan of the first edition.
# STATUS: VERIFIED against an edition by Michelle Opitz, 2026-10-17. Read from the MIDI first and checked against standard theory and a printed edition (R-092). A hand reading of tests/fixtures/framework-v1-corpus/"Mozart 545.mid" (the top line and the bass of each measure, dumped beat by beat; the first movement is its first 146 measures, with both repeats written out),
# written before the verification test was run and NOT derived from the output of any analysis stage. Where the older annotation
# files for this piece (key regions, cadences, phrase form) cover the same ground their values are copied here, and
# framework_v1_fixture_consistency checks that the two agree.
#
# Every list below is COMPLETE for its scope: a cadence the music does not have is a claim, not an omission, so a cadence the chain
# reports inside the cadence scope that is not listed is reported as a deviation. (Phrase ends, themes, expansions and
# returns are checked only as listed: the form readings say what could be read with confidence.)
#
# FORMAT, one per line (blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored):
#   piece <id>
#   meter <beats per measure> <beat length as a fraction of a whole note>
#   home <tonic> <major|minor>                          the piece's key
#   keys-scope <first> <last>                           the measures the chain runs over; the key regions are checked here
#   region <first> <last> <tonic> <major|minor>         the key of those measures (a region is two measures or more; a passing one-measure tonicization is not one)
#   unscored <first> <last>                             measures left out of the key check
#   change <measure> <extent> [return]                  the key change that STARTS at this measure; extent is tonicization, extended-tonicization,
#                                                       weak-modulation or modulation (a cadence in the new key that the music then leaves is a weak
#                                                       modulation); 'return' marks the change back to the key before the excursion
#   cadence-scope <first> <last>                        the measures whose cadences are listed
#   cadence <measure> <beat> <pac|iac|hc|deceptive|plagal|subverted>   the cadence whose ARRIVAL chord starts here (beats are 1-based)
#   cadence <measure> <beat> <type> optional           the same, but the music may or may not have it: missing is no deviation, and found with its type
#                                                       (within one beat) it is not an extra
#   readings <measure> <beat> <reading> <measure> <beat> <reading> [prefer 1|2]
#                                                       one cadence point with two competing readings (a V to I6 evaded or prolonged, a dominant
#                                                       before a section start as a half or an authentic cadence); a reading is a cadence type word
#                                                       or 'prolongation'. The chain's primary and alternative reading must be these two, in either
#                                                       order, each arrival within one beat. 'prefer 1' or 'prefer 2' also requires that reading to
#                                                       have the higher share. A result a readings line takes is not an extra and matches no
#                                                       'cadence' line; a phrase-end at either reading's measure passes at either measure
#   form-scope <first> <last>
#   phrase-end <measure> <pac|iac|hc>                   a phrase ends in this measure (the measure its arrival chord ends in)
#   theme <form> <first> <last> [parts <a-first> <a-last> <b-first> <b-last>]   a theme and its two parts
#   expansion <internal|contraction|external> <first> <last> <measures>
#   original <name> <first> <last>                      a theme that later returns (thematic returns)
#   return <name> <first> <last>                        a later statement of the original called <name>
#
# Tolerances (the verification test): a key region's edges and a phrase end or a theme edge are matched within one measure; a cadence's
# arrival within one beat and its type exactly (PAC and IAC are different types).

piece mozart545
meter 4 1/4
home C major
keys-scope 1 146
# copied from mozart545_key_regions.txt (the development, 57-69 and 102-114, is not scored); the extent of each change is the one the music has.
# The recapitulation keys (C major for m79-101 and m124-146, with the half cadence on G at m85 and m130) are accepted and flagged for Michelle to re-verify. M79-85
# repeats m6-12 note for note. The C-sharp in m13 is a chromatic line D, C-sharp, C, B into the second theme, not a change of key by itself.
region 1 12 C major
region 13 28 G major
region 29 40 C major
region 41 56 G major
unscored 57 69
region 70 78 F major
region 79 101 C major
unscored 102 114
region 115 123 F major
region 124 146 C major
change 13 modulation
change 29 modulation
change 41 modulation
change 79 modulation
change 124 modulation
# the exposition (1-28): a half cadence on V at measure 12 (a G major triad, V of C, after I-IV-I-IV over the G pedal in m11), then the closing section in G major
# (copied from mozart545_cadences.txt): m26 and m27 are codettas before the closing perfect authentic cadence at m28, so their cadences are optional (R-095) and the one at
# m28 is required; the repeat starts at measure 29
cadence-scope 1 28
cadence 12 1 hc
cadence 26 1 pac optional
cadence 27 1 pac optional
cadence 28 1 pac
readings 4 1 subverted 4 1 prolongation
form-scope 1 28
# no cadence ends the four-measure opening (measure 4 reaches I6): the first phrase runs to the half cadence that sounds into measure 12; the exposition closes at 28
phrase-end 12 hc
phrase-end 28 pac
# thematic returns over the whole movement (keys-scope). The main theme is measures 1-4 and returns in the written-out repeat (29), and in the
# recapitulation, which opens in F major (70) and again in its repeat (115). The second theme is measures 14-17 (G major) and returns in the repeat (42),
# in C major in the recapitulation (87) and in its repeat (132).
original main 1 4
return main 29 32
return main 70 73
return main 115 118
original second 14 17
return second 42 45
return second 87 90
return second 132 135
